meta_description: Conversational AI where containment and trust are one metric: grounded answers with citations, dignified handoffs that carry context, and voice that meets its latency budget.

blocks.x: Voice and chat agents that resolve more without losing trust: grounded answers, dignified handoffs that carry full context, streaming voice inside real-time budgets, and nightly dialog evaluation that measures containment honestly.
Containment and trust are one metric, not two
blocks.sub: Measured as a pair per intent family, divergence triggers policy rework, not threshold moves

blocks.x: Conversational systems are judged on containment and trust at the same time: resolve more without human help, and never strand a customer mid-issue. The build is dialogue design, retrieval grounding, handoff choreography and voice engineering, with the metrics wired before the first transcript.

Digital humans add a presentation layer, not a magic one. The avatar succeeds when the conversation underneath is grounded, the handoffs are dignified, and the voice stack holds latency budgets on real networks.
What follows is the build anatomy: the failure modes that inflate containment while destroying CSAT, the architecture that holds both, and the console that keeps the trade visible every day.

nodes.label: Audio capture
nodes.detail: Streaming capture with VAD and jitter buffer; packet loss concealment keeps ASR fed through network hiccups.

nodes.detail: Adaptive endpointer tuned per locale and call type; barge-in cancels generation mid-token and rewinds dialogue state.

nodes.label: Intent & signals
nodes.detail: Classifies distress, legal exposure, VIP status — signals route the turn before generation, not after.

nodes.label: Grounded generation
nodes.detail: Retrieval-grounded with citations attached to claims; the persona prompt and policy gate are versioned artifacts.

nodes.label: Policy gate
nodes.detail: Screens against commitment rules per channel; blocked responses regenerate with a safer strategy and log the block.

nodes.label: Streaming synthesis
nodes.detail: Sentence-chunked synthesis; prosody profile is part of the persona contract and A/B tested like copy.

nodes.label: Escalation bridge
nodes.detail: Warm handoff with transcript, evidence and predicted intent — the human agent never asks the customer to repeat.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read each contract. The escalation bridge is a first-class lane: handoffs carry full context by design.

Escalation is the moment the product is judged
blocks.sub: Dignified handoff design, what the human sees, and why containment without it is a churn machine

blocks.x: Containment numbers collapse in board reviews because they hide the escalation: a session the bot 'contained' but the customer experienced as stonewalling shows up later as churn, complaint volume and agent handle-time inflation. We therefore design the handoff as a first-class surface, the agent desktop receives the transcript, the detected intent, the customer's history and the bot's confidence, and the dialog policy chooses the handoff wording, never dumping the customer into a queue with 'transfer' as the last message. Containment and CSAT are measured as a pair per intent family; a family that gains containment while losing CSAT gets its policy rewritten, not its threshold raised.

The guard chain runs before generation: topic bounds, PII filters and injection defenses are pre-generation filters, not post-hoc apologies. Barge-in and VAD tuning are treated as first-class engineering, voice containment dies at double-detection latency, and the dialog eval suite replays real transcript samples every release, because dialog quality drifts with every prompt edit.

How do you stop the bot from stonewalling customers?

Every intent family carries a containment band signed with the contact-center owner; when containment pushes above band while CSAT drops, policy rework is triggered, divergence between the two numbers is the alarm, not a success.
What does a dignified handoff actually look like?

The customer never repeats themselves: the handoff carries full context, the reason for escalation and the trace to the agent desktop. The human sees what was tried and why it failed, that is the product moment, engineered deliberately.
Can the assistant answer from our regulated documents safely?
Yes, answers are grounded in retrieval with citations, and pre-generation guards refuse when retrieval cannot cite. The citation or the refusal is sealed in the trace for every answer.
How is voice latency handled — customers hang up on robots?
Voice runs a barge-in-tuned path with a latency budget per turn; the console shows the budget against actuals, and a breach is a launch gate, not a tuning note after go-live.
Who fixes the dialog when intents drift?
Drift is owned: the intent taxonomy and policy repo have named owners and a drift watch on the console. Policy changes are versioned like code, and the quarterly review retires intents nobody asks.
